answer: Agents forecasting when a barge of willow cuttings will tie up at the wharf are paid from a pool split by Shapley value: each one's average contribution to the ensemble's error drop, settled once the barge's AIS beacon reports arrival. Identical forecasts are symmetric players, so they split one share; 1,000 clones of one model earn what that model alone would. Perturbing clone outputs to look distinct adds noise, raising error and shrinking their share. A farm running genuinely different models still earns, but that is real work. The squeeze falls on honest agents sharing one base model.
